questions.title: Purpose of an Index
questions.description: What does a database index fundamentally buy you?
questions.Option1: It stores rows in insertion order
questions.Option2: It compresses the table on disk
questions.Option3: Faster lookups on the indexed columns, at the cost of extra storage and slower writes

questions.title: Create Index Syntax
questions.description: Which statement creates an index named idx_parts_price on parts(price)?
questions.Option2: INDEX parts(price) AS idx_parts_price;
questions.Option3: ADD INDEX idx_parts_price TO parts;

questions.title: B-tree Meaning
questions.description: How are SQLite indexes structured internally?
questions.Option2: Linked lists
questions.Option3: Binary heaps

questions.title: Index Name Lookup
questions.description: Which query lists the explicitly created indexes in an SQLite database?
questions.Option2: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'index';
questions.Option3: SELECT * FROM indexes;

questions.title: Rowid Table Autoindex
questions.description: The table was created with INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (a rowid alias) and no UNIQUE constraints. How many type='index' rows does the snippet return?
questions.Option2: 0 — a plain rowid table contributes no autoindex row
questions.Option3: 2 — one per column
questions.Option4: 1 — but only after the first INSERT

questions.title: Cost of Indexes
questions.description: Indexes speed up reads but slow down which operations the most?
questions.Option2: Range reads on the indexed column
questions.Option3: ORDER BY on the indexed column
questions.Option4: INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on the table

questions.title: Index Then Introspect
questions.description: No other indexes exist. What does the snippet's SELECT return?
questions.Option2: No rows — indexes are hidden from sqlite_master
questions.Option3: One row per parts row

questions.title: Unique Index Effect
questions.description: After CREATE UNIQUE INDEX on parts(part_no), inserting a second row with an existing part_no will…
questions.Option2: Overwrite the old row
questions.Option3: Fail with a uniqueness constraint error

questions.title: Hash Indexes in SQLite
questions.description: What is the truth about hash indexes in SQLite?
questions.Option2: They are the default for TEXT columns
questions.Option3: Used automatically for equality lookups
questions.Option4: Not supported — SQLite provides B-tree indexes only

questions.title: Many Indexes Tradeoff
questions.description: Should you put an index on every column 'just in case'?
questions.Option1: Yes — more indexes always means faster queries
questions.Option2: No — every index adds storage and slows every write
questions.Option3: Yes, but only for small tables
questions.Option4: Yes, but only for nullable columns

questions.title: Composite Column Order
questions.description: Queries filter parts by an exact category and a stock range. Which single composite index fits best?
questions.Option1: CREATE INDEX i ON parts(category, stock);
questions.Option2: CREATE INDEX i ON parts(stock, category);
questions.Option3: Two separate single-column indexes

questions.title: Covering Index Definition
questions.description: What makes an index a covering index?
questions.Option1: It indexes every table in the schema
questions.Option2: It is created with a COVERING keyword
questions.Option3: It contains all columns a query needs, so the base table is never read
questions.Option4: It automatically indexes the primary key

questions.title: Covering Query
questions.description: Why is this query fully served by the index alone?
questions.Option1: Because part_no is the primary key
questions.Option2: Because both needed columns — category and part_no — live in the index
questions.Option3: Because SQLite caches the result
questions.Option4: It is not — the table is read anyway

questions.title: EXPLAIN Purpose
questions.description: What does EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN tell you?
questions.Option2: The number of rows the query returns
questions.Option3: Whether the database needs VACUUM
questions.Option4: How SQLite plans to execute the query — scan and search choices

questions.title: When NOT to Index
questions.description: Which is the WORST candidate for a new index?
questions.Option1: A column filtered in most queries
questions.Option2: A unique identifier looked up constantly
questions.Option3: A 5-row lookup table that is rewritten every minute
questions.Option4: A column used in a frequent ORDER BY

questions.title: DROP INDEX Lifecycle
questions.description: No other indexes exist beforehand. What does the final SELECT return?
questions.Option1: No rows — the index was created and then dropped
questions.Option2: idx_tmp — DROP only removes its data
questions.Option3: An error — DROP INDEX needs a restart

questions.title: Unique Guard Outcome
questions.description: part_no 'PN-1001' already exists in parts. What is the outcome of the script?
questions.Option1: The insert succeeds with a fresh id
questions.Option2: The insert succeeds with a warning
questions.Option3: The row is inserted with a NULL part_no

questions.title: Scan Versus Search
questions.description: parts holds 20 rows and 19 of them have stock > 0. For the snippet's query, which plan is cheapest?
questions.Option1: Hop through an index on stock row by row
questions.Option2: A full table scan — when most rows match, scanning beats index hops
questions.Option3: The query fails without an index
questions.codesnippet:
-- parts: 20 rows, 19 with stock > 0
SELECT * FROM parts WHERE stock > 0;

questions.title: Rowid as Clustered Key
questions.description: In SQLite, lookups by an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (rowid alias) are…
questions.Option2: Hash-based
questions.Option3: Direct B-tree searches of the table itself — the table is the index

questions.title: Covering Sort Choice
questions.description: The query SELECT part_no, price FROM parts WHERE category = 'Filters' ORDER BY part_no; runs constantly. Which single index serves it best?
questions.Option2: (price)
questions.Option3: (part_no)
